comment: MS-DOS + Windows for Workgroups 3.11 VirtualBox VM with Borland Turbo C++ 3.0 (C:\TURBOC). Tests both DOS ports:
the 8086 real mode one (BGI Scene Editor, menu only) and the 80286 protected mode one (raytracer, RAY286.BIN).
RULE: everything an agent creates goes inside C:\VITRAL. Never leave files or folders outside C:\VITRAL
(no scratch files in C:\, C:\NETDOS, C:\TURBOC or C:\DOSVIEW; do not edit AUTOEXEC.BAT or CONFIG.SYS without asking).
RULE: never copy the whole repository to a DOS machine: disk space is limited. Copy only etc/ and turboc/,
mapped to 8.3 names (turboc/scripts/stageDosFull.sh), never etc/portMachines.
nodes.cpu: VirtualBox x86 (runs the 8086 and the 286 builds)

comment: Normal medium: an ISO with one VITRAL.TGZ, put in the IDE port 1 device 0 CD drive (D: in DOS, MSCDEX) without rebooting:
VBoxManage storageattach DOS --storagectl IDE --port 1 --device 0 --type dvddrive --medium <iso>.
Extract in C:\VITRAL with C:\NETDOS\DJTAR -x D:\VITRAL.TGZ (djtar, GO32 and CWSDPMI of DJGPP).
For a few changed files, send a small TGZ with only them, delete the old copies first (djtar does not overwrite).
mTCP FTP.EXE (C:\NETDOS) and floppies are not for source trees (see turboc/README.md).
VirtualBox VRDE (VNC), no password. VBoxManage controlvm DOS keyboardputstring/keyboardputscancode 1c 9c (Enter)
and screenshotpng drive the console without VNC; type in chunks of about 12 characters.
mTCP TELNETD (192.168.1.250:23, no password, C:\NETDOS\README.TXT) only answers while it is running.

layout.C:\\VITRAL\\ETC: 8.3 copy of etc/ (plus the scenes of the raytracer RUN*.BAT at its top)
layout.C:\\TURBOC: Turbo C++ 3.0 and BGI drivers (C:\TURBOC\BGI); read only
layout.C:\\NETDOS: djtar and mTCP network tools; read only

nodes.toolchain: Borland Turbo C++ 3.0 (tcc, tlink, tlib, tasm)

comment: The minimalistic Vitral kernel (cpp/x86_64_smp_kernel), built from the cpp port and booted in QEMU.
The run scripts must be executed with sudo (bridged network); build first as the normal user with -n.
Tested from Linux Ubuntu 22.04 (x86_64 host) and macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 (Apple M1 host).

comment: Debian 1.1 "Buzz" i386 VirtualBox VM (Linux 2.0.0, libc5, gcc 2.7.2.1, GNU make 3.75, XFree86 3.x, LessTif mwm, Mesa 3.0).
Tests the turboc port with its legacy Makefiles (no CMake): turboc/scripts/compileWithMake.sh.
Rules: copy only etc/ and turboc/ (never etc/portMachines); build in the background (nohup make) and poll,
as a telnet login takes minutes while the machine compiles; its clock is ahead of the host, so touch the
extracted files before an incremental make; root only through su (the root password is not stored here).
nodes.cpu: VirtualBox i386, 127 MB of RAM (lilo append mem=127M), no swap
nodes.toolchain: gcc 2.7.2.1, GNU make 3.75 (turboc/legacy.mk), X11R6 Xt/Xaw/LessTif, Mesa 3.0 (OpenGL 1.2)

comment: FTP with the user and password of this node; paths are relative to ~jedilink (curl -T <file> ftp://vmdebian/<path>).
Send one tar.gz made with tar --format=gnu of git ls-files -co --exclude-standard of turboc/ and etc/, and unpack it
with gzip -dc x.tgz | tar xf -. Its GNU tar 1.11 silently drops members whose path has exactly 100 characters:
put those in a second archive made from a shorter base folder. Wait until the upload is complete before extracting.
Telnet with the user and password of this node runs the builds and the tests; X programs use DISPLAY=:0, the
xdm session of jedilink on the VM console. Visual check: VirtualBox VRDE (VNC) of the VM on the VirtualBox host,
port 5901 (the port of the VM settings), with the password below.

tests.comment: Pass: every MIT scene of runAll.sh renders a .ppm, and an MCP session (TCP 1234) builds a scene with bodies and a light and renders it with OpenGL, raytracing, wireframe and APPEL hidden lines.
sceneEditor: MCP client: line-delimited JSON-RPC on vmdebian:1234 (initialize, tools/list, tools/call)
